title: Make the two children of a node

blocks.text: The depot model's search has found a fractional variable at a node and must split the node in two. A node is described by its bounds: a dict that maps each integer variable's name to a pair `(lo, hi)`, meaning $`\text{lo} \le x \le \text{hi}`$.
Write `children(bounds, name, value)` in `children.py`. `value` is the LP value of variable `name` at this node, and it is fractional. Return a pair `(down, up)` of new bounds dicts:
where `(lo, hi)` are the node's bounds on `name`. Every other variable keeps its bounds in both children. The caller keeps the node's own `bounds` to log it, so leave that dict as it was.

from __future__ import annotations

import math


def children(bounds: dict[str, tuple[int, int]], name: str, value: float):
    """The down and up children of a node, split on `name` at its fractional LP value."""
    lo, hi = bounds[name]
    down = dict(bounds)
    down[name] = (lo, math.floor(value))
    up = dict(bounds)
    up[name] = (math.ceil(value), hi)
    return down, up


if __name__ == "__main__":
    node = {"trucks_north": (0, 8), "open_south": (0, 1)}
    print(children(node, "trucks_north", 2.75))

print("node:", node)
down, up = children(node, "vans", 5.3)
print("split vans at 5.3, down:", down)
print("split vans at 5.3, up:", up)
down, up = children(node, "shift", -0.6)
print("split shift at -0.6, down:", down["shift"], "up:", up["shift"])
print("node after the splits:", node)

cases.says: a 0-1 variable at 0.4 gives the children x <= 0 and x >= 1
a count at 3.6 with bounds 0..10 gives 0..3 and 4..10
every other variable's bounds are copied unchanged into both children
with bounds 2..9 and value 4.5 the down child keeps its lower bound 2 and the up child its upper bound 9
a value of -1.5 gives x <= -2 and x >= -1
the parent's bounds dict is the same after the call

origin.section: A General Integer Branches on Floor and Ceiling

concepts: a child is the parent's LP with one bound changed, and its LP value is never above the parent's
a general integer at a fractional value v splits into x <= floor(v) and x >= ceil(v)
branching puts every integer plan in exactly one child and the fractional LP point in neither
